newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher for 4th straight session.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher for 4th straight session.

text.p: Active buying on financials pushed Taiwan share prices to a higher close on Thursday, marking the market's fourth straight session of gains, brokers said.
The index ended 52.29 points or 0.61 percent higher at 8,629.23. Turnover was a brisk T$145.1 billion.

Financials, which had lagged other sectors during the recent bull run, rose 3.0 percent with the "Big Three" state-run banks surging in reaction to the government's privatisation programme for the three banks, brokers said.
Chang Hwa Bank surged T$7.5 to T$123, while both First Commercial and Hua Nan Bank rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$124 and T$118, respectively.
"Most analysts estimate the future underwriting price of the Big Three would be around T$130 each, so their prices have much potential to rise," said Capital Securities manager Alex Chiu.
Earlier in April the Taiwan provincial government said it would speed the selldown of its Big Three equity from 18 months to 14 months.
HSBC James Capel analyst Stephen Wang said financials would be one of three main sectors to lead the market's overall upward swing in the near term.
The others were electronics and constructions.
Steel and transport shares also rose on Thursday, but most other sectors saw profit-taking.
Electronics, which had surged for three previous sessions, fell 0.52 percent with Taiwan Semiconductor losing T$2.5 to T$88.
Foods fell 1.29 percent after farm officials said they feared a deadly disease on the island's chicken population may be breaking out.
Brokers said they expected heavy resistance to emerge around the 8,650-8,700 level.
"Any further rise would become risky as it would not be backed up by sound economic fundamentals," Wang said.
Wang added that the central bank likely would launch measures to cool the market if it rose too much.
A 8,560-8,700 range was seen for Friday.
